Summary: WT-5461 Search should not return onpage value if nothing is found by transaction read
Status: Closed
GA Released For OM/CM: Yes - 07/02/2020 (2454 Days Ago)
Assignee: Chenhao Qu

issuetype.description: A task that needs to be done.

fields.description:
Before durable history, we store the stable version in the disk image. The transaction read only traverse the update chain and the upper level search logic has the assumption that if nothing is found by transaction read, we should return the onpage value.

This is no longer true in history store as we store the newest committed value on disk. To change that, we have modified transaction read to traverse the update chain, onpage value, then the update chain. However, we haven't removed the assumption in the upper level search logic that the onpage value should be visible if nothing is found. This problem is causing test_hs02 to fail.

comments.body: This is failing because we are not returning tombstone in txn_read if nothing is visible.

bq. This is failing because we are not returning tombstone in txn_read if nothing is visible.

[~chenhao.qu] what are we returning instead? On the surface it seems like returning nothing is the right thing to do if nothing is visible?
In the current search framework, if we return nothing from txn_read, we will return the onpage value instead.
After returning tombstone, this test passes but some other tests are failing.

bq. In the current search framework, if we return nothing from txn_read, we will return the onpage value instead.

How do we know that the on page value is visible?

We don't. Before durable history, the search sequence is update chain, history store, and onpage value. Now we changed it to update chain, onpage value, and history store. However, we haven't changed the search framework accordingly and the upper level read logic still returns onpage value is nothing is found. There is a separate ticket for that I think. [~alex.cameron] knows better about this.

Yeah. Returning a tombstone out {{wt_txn_read}} caused some fallout since it didn't make sense for some of the callers. Now that I've extracted the update list iteration part into {{wt_txn_read_upd_list}} which we're using for the insert list, this situation might be better now so it's worth trying to return a tombstone again.

The ticket that [~chenhao.qu] is referring to is WT-5470.

checkpoint_integrity test is still failing. The test starts a subprocess to run some operations in wiredtiger and injects failures to checkpoint. It expects we still be able to recover the data after that. However, with WT-5461 change, checkpoint does fail but goes into panic state and killing the subprocess.
In pm-1521 branch, I see the same behaviour that the subprocess crash but we still be able to read the data due to we return the onpage value as default.
In develop, the subprocess also crashes so I think it is expected.
So the problem is why sometimes we cannot see any data after restart from checkpoint failure.
Odd thing is that wt dump actually returns data on the failed database. I suspect something similar to the backup write_gen problem (WT-5516).
